chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Musa al-Nawfali, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So the freeing of a believing slave.' He said: 'It means one who acknowledges [the faith].'

key_terms.رَقَبَةٍ: slave (specifically a slave owned by a non-Muslim or a mukatab in some contexts, often used for manumission)
key_terms.مُؤْمِنَةٍ: believing (female form, referring to the slave)

ai.seo_question: What does 'believing slave' mean in the context of freeing slaves for expiation?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'believing' (mu'min) in the context of freeing a slave for expiation is clarified as 'muqirrah,' meaning one who acknowledges or professes the faith. This interpretation emphasizes the spiritual status of the slave rather than just their legal condition, aligning with the Shia emphasis on internal conviction in acts of worship. The ruling underscores the merit of freeing a slave who is already recognized within the fold of Islam, thereby facilitating their spiritual and social integration.
